records.name: Peter Neumann
records.bio: Neumann is repeatedly credited for photographs in the Tübingen Blaschka sourcebook and object records. His images provide a substantial modern visual-documentation layer for model comparison, condition and catalogue work.

records.name: Dante Abate
records.bio: Abate took part in the 13–17 February 2017 digital-documentation campaign at the Fondazione Scienza e Tecnica in Florence. With Sorin Hermon and the Cyprus Institute, he helped document approximately fifteen Blaschka objects using object-specific 3D methods within the E-RIHS framework.
records.open: The public source does not verify that the 3D campaign was extended from the initial group to the complete collection.

records.name: Sorin Hermon
records.bio: Hermon took part in the February 2017 3D-documentation campaign at the Fondazione Scienza e Tecnica with Dante Abate and the Cyprus Institute. The project adapted documentation to differences in form, technique and glass type across approximately fifteen Blaschka objects.
records.open: The public source does not verify that the initial campaign reached the whole collection.

records.name: Carl Bento
records.bio: Bento is credited in the Australian Museum’s photographic record MA817 and in reference photography attached to Blaschka object documentation. The project keeps MA817 as a photographic or archive identifier rather than treating it automatically as a physical-object number.

records.name: James Balodimas
records.bio: Balodimas is credited for the Field Museum’s 1993 photograph of its Blaschka Tethys fimbria model, preserved under photo-archive identifier Z94040c. That image is one of the project’s direct modern anchors for the Ward and World’s Columbian Exposition collection history.
records.open: The local Field Museum inventory number and full object record remain to be linked to the photographic anchor.

records.name: Gary Hodges
records.bio: Hodges is repeatedly credited as the photographer or visual source in the Cornell-linked catalogue index used by the project. Those credits attach modern images to specific Blaschka numbers and taxa and therefore form part of the collection’s digital documentation layer.
records.open: The backend field combines photographer and source credits, so no broader photographic role is inferred beyond the credited records.

records.name: Kent Loeffler
records.bio: Loeffler is repeatedly named in the Cornell-linked catalogue index as photographer or visual source for individual Blaschka records. The project retains those credits because the images are part of the modern object-identification and comparison infrastructure.
records.open: The backend field combines photographer and source credits, so no broader role is inferred beyond the credited records.

records.name: Claire Smith
records.bio: Smith is credited as photographer or visual source for several Cornell-linked Blaschka catalogue records, including object images used in cross-collection comparison. Her record is limited to those documented image-source credits.
records.open: The backend does not yet provide a fuller authority identification for Claire Smith.

records.name: J. E. Gray
records.bio: A verified Natural History Museum archival reference records Frederick Wollaston Hutton writing to J. E. Gray on 26 July 1874. The reference places Gray in the Otago-to-British-Museum zoological network, but the contents have not yet been captured and the project does not treat the letter as Blaschka-specific correspondence.
records.open: Letter contents remain uncaptured; a Blaschka-specific connection is therefore unproven.

records.name: Robert Etheridge
records.bio: An Australian Museum archival reference records Hutton writing to Robert Etheridge on 21 August 1877. It establishes an Otago–Australian Museum exchange connection, but the letter contents have not been captured and no Blaschka-specific subject is inferred from the reference alone.
records.open: Letter contents remain uncaptured; the edge is contextual to the Otago collection network rather than proven Blaschka correspondence.
